# manager.predictor.get_model_prediction { #spotforecast2_safe.manager.predictor.get_model_prediction }

```python
manager.predictor.get_model_prediction(
    model_name,
    model_dir=None,
    predict_size=None,
)
```

Get the prediction package from the latest trained model.

This function retrieves the latest iteration of a specified model from the
cache and calls its `package_prediction` method to obtain a comprehensive
set of predictions and metrics.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type                                                                                             | Description                                                                       | Default    |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| model_name   | [str](`str`)                                                                                     | Name of the model to use (e.g., 'lgbm', 'xgb', 'catboost').                       | _required_ |
| model_dir    | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[Union](`typing.Union`)\[[str](`str`), [Path](`pathlib.Path`)\]\] | Directory where models are stored. If None, defaults to the library's cache home. | `None`     |
| predict_size | [Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[int](`int`)\]                                                    | Optional override for the prediction horizon.                                     | `None`     |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                       | Description                                                 |
|--------|------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | A dictionary containing predictions and metrics produced by |
|        | [Dict](`typing.Dict`)\[[str](`str`), [Any](`typing.Any`)\] | `package_prediction()`.                                     |

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                                               | Description                                                                                                           |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [FileNotFoundError](`FileNotFoundError`)           | If no trained model is found for `model_name` in `model_dir`.                                                         |
|        | [AttributeError](`AttributeError`)                 | If the loaded model does not implement a `package_prediction` method.                                                 |
|        | [PredictionPackageError](`PredictionPackageError`) | If `package_prediction()` itself fails — see `forecaster.wrappers.model.ForecasterRecursiveModel.package_prediction`. |
|        | [OSError](`OSError`)                               | If the on-disk model file exists but cannot be deserialised (corrupt joblib).                                         |

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

`predict_size` is accepted by `get_model_prediction()` but only has effect if the concrete model's `package_prediction()` accepts it.
The original `ForecasterRecursiveModel.package_prediction()` does not — so this parameter is currently forward-looking API design, not yet wired end-to-end.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```{python}
import tempfile
from spotforecast2_safe.manager.predictor import get_model_prediction

# When no model has been trained, get_model_prediction raises FileNotFoundError.
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    try:
        get_model_prediction("lgbm", model_dir=tmpdir)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        print(type(e).__name__)
        assert "lgbm" in str(e)
```
